model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Lee: a D+10 seat, incumbency, and a lopsided financial advantage over a barely funded challenger. Markets agree, pricing her near 97%, so the race stays firmly in Safe D territory.
model.watch: A major outside spending surge for Hayes or a polling surprise showing a single-digit race would be the main signal to revisit this rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Summer Lee seeks a third term in a Pittsburgh-area district that leans Democratic by about ten points. She enters the general election with a large financial edge, having raised roughly $1.5 million and holding $1.6 million on hand, while Republican James Hayes has raised about $40,000. No outside groups have invested meaningfully against her, and no public polls of the race are available.

With no expert ratings or surveys to lean on, the picture rests on fundamentals and market pricing, both of which favor Lee heavily. Prediction markets put her chances near 97 percent. The seat is rated Safe D, with the usual caveat that thin data leaves somewhat wider uncertainty than a well-polled race would.
